howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.lead: Four steps from your mailbox to the public database.

steps.title: Submit your cards
steps.body: Tell us what you are sending — name, set, set number and release year for each card. Add a photo if you have one.

steps.title: Ship to the vault
steps.body: Pack your cards and send them with the shipping label we generate. Every arrival is logged and photographed.

steps.title: Authenticate and grade
steps.body: Our experts confirm the card is genuine, then score its condition against the published grading scale.

steps.title: Seal and return
steps.body: The card is sealed in a tamper-evident slab and shipped back to you. The result joins the public database.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Everything we are asked most often. If your question is not here, contact us.

items.question: How long does grading take?
items.answer: Turnaround depends on the service level you choose at submission. You can track your order's status from your account at every stage.

items.question: What grading scale do you use?
items.answer: Cards are scored on a numeric scale covering centering, corners, edges and surface, and the sub-grades are shown on the label alongside the overall grade.

items.question: What is the difference between grading and authentication?
items.answer: Authentication confirms a card is genuine. Grading scores the physical condition of a card we have authenticated. You can order either or both.

items.question: Are my cards insured while you have them?
items.answer: Cards are insured from the moment they are logged at the vault until they are handed back to the carrier for return shipping.

items.question: What happens if a card is damaged in your care?
items.answer: If we damage a card while it is in our care, we refund the grading fee and the card's declared value.

items.question: Will my cards appear in the public database?
items.answer: Yes. Every card we grade or authenticate enters the public Pop Report once the result is finalised, so collectors can see how many examples exist at each grade.
